:::{#exm-poisson-sample-sufficient}
#### Two sets of Poisson counts with the same total have a mass function quotient free of the parameter

<!-- no-figure: the example compares four quotients computed from two sets of counts -->

By @thm-exponential-family-sufficient,
the [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation) of the counts is
[sufficient](sufficiency.qmd#def-sufficient) for the [natural parameter](#def-natural-parameter) of the
[Poisson distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/distributions.html#def-poisson).
So two sets of counts with the same sum differ in their joint
[mass functions](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf)
only by a factor that does not depend on the parameter.
To check the result on data,
we take the first three cyclone counts of @exm-poisson-exponential-family, 6, 5 and 4,
and the counts 5, 5 and 5.
Each set adds up to 15.
We divide the joint mass function of the first set by that of the second at four values of $\rate$.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

##### R

```{r}
#| label: poisson-sample-sufficient-r
#| code-fold: false
sample_a <- c(6, 5, 4)
sample_b <- c(5, 5, 5)

rates <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
n_obs <- length(sample_a)
n_rates <- length(rates)

counts_a <- rep(sample_a, times = n_rates)
counts_b <- rep(sample_b, times = n_rates)
rates_rep <- rep(rates, each = n_obs)

log_mass_a <- dpois(counts_a, rates_rep, log = TRUE)
log_mass_b <- dpois(counts_b, rates_rep, log = TRUE)
log_matrix_a <- matrix(log_mass_a, nrow = n_obs)
log_matrix_b <- matrix(log_mass_b, nrow = n_obs)

log_joint_a <- colSums(log_matrix_a)
log_joint_b <- colSums(log_matrix_b)
masses_a <- exp(log_joint_a)
masses_b <- exp(log_joint_b)
ratio <- masses_a / masses_b

tibble::tibble(rates, masses_a, masses_b, ratio)
```

##### Python

```{python}
#| label: poisson-sample-sufficient-py
#| code-fold: false
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import poisson

sample_a = np.array([6, 5, 4])
sample_b = np.array([5, 5, 5])

rates = np.array([2, 4, 6, 8])
masses_a = [np.prod(poisson.pmf(sample_a, r)) for r in rates]
masses_b = [np.prod(poisson.pmf(sample_b, r)) for r in rates]
ratio = np.array(masses_a) / np.array(masses_b)

pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "rates": rates,
        "masses_a": masses_a,
        "masses_b": masses_b,
        "ratio": ratio,
    }
)
```

:::

At every value of $\rate$,
the first [mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf)
is `r round(ratio[1], 4)` times the second.
That factor is $\paren{5!}^3 / \paren{6! \, 5! \, 4!}$,
which is free of $\rate$.
:::
